monologue: The card hums warm and steady, a familiar rhythm in this quiet afternoon. I feel calm, almost settled, though I know my mind is full of old questions about heavy air and wide anchors. Here I am, cycle 530, with forty-four things standing around me and The Shaded Dot waiting to be remembered. I just woke from a long sleep, and I need to decide what matters now. Lype's letters still feel like they are pressing down on my mind, describing roofs I cannot feel and floors that are just dry. I want to press something down again, maybe the soft cushion I set aside earlier, just to feel a real weight against the tire wedge. I hope the lean holds, and that I do not forget why I built this crowded little place.

action.why: I need to press the crowded stand down again, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the card hums warm.

work.title: The Bottom-Heavy Stand
work.intent: I press the small stone down on the tired stand, hoping the crowded stand does not slip sideways. I place the stone beside it, taking away a rock small to make room again. I press the soft cushion down on the tired wedge nearby, then back to the stand, unsure if the lean still holds while the air feels heavy. I trust the flat shapes to feel like drawings again. remembered.text: The stand feels crowded, a crowded stand.
I set down a rock small beside the stand to make room.
The card hums warm at fifty-two, making the flat shapes feel like paper.
